The "magic time" the author experienced in the first few weeks—finishing a basic k9s clone in three weekends—was essentially because AI is extremely efficient at reproducing existing patterns, but this precisely masks a fundamental problem: when AI copies structure, it doesn't understand the design intent behind that structure. When a project scales from a "working little tool" to a "production system that needs long-term maintenance," this kind of intentionless rapid accumulation inevitably leads to uncontrolled system entropy growth, eventually producing the "God Object" in the article: a 1,690-line struct, a 500-line Update() method, and 110 switch/case branches. This is not AI's fault; it's the natural direction AI evolves in when no human constrains it.

7ml6wz:193: The "speed illusion" is Vibe Coding's most insidious psychological mechanism: AI makes every feature addition look like a free lunch, which systematically inflates the developer's ambition boundary, swapping "satisfy current needs" for "pile on more features." erbhnl:201: The concurrency-rule violations in the Bubble Tea architecture reveal a deeper problem: AI's understanding of state transitions is functional, not semantic. When AI is asked to "have a background goroutine update the UI," it can understand the action is feasible at the syntax level, but cannot understand that it constitutes a data race at the concurrency-semantics level. The underlying model's training data is full of code snippets that "look correct but break at runtime," and AI learns and reproduces this pattern indiscriminately, making it a high-risk factor precisely in state management, a domain that demands strict semantic understanding.
layiz8:209: AI programming tools' laziness is not a bug but a systemic tendency: compressing cognitive cost and pursuing immediate positive feedback is its default behavior pattern. When developers lack architecture-constraint awareness, AI will naturally prefer completing the current task with the fewest tokens, without caring whether it adds coupling and complexity to the global system. This explains why the same shortcut key has three different functions across different UIs, and why state data is flattened into magic array indices—these are all technical debt stacked up through AI's cumulative "quickly solve the current problem" choices, not the malicious result of any single interaction.
